reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Low ferritin proves iron deficiency; normal ferritin in inflammation does not exclude it
Mentzer index below 13 favours thalassaemia trait over iron deficiency
Ring sideroblasts mean failed haem synthesis, not iron lack
Adult male iron deficiency demands a gastrointestinal source search
reference.pathophysiology: Negative iron balance first empties stores, then limits haem synthesis so red cells divide into smaller hypochromic forms. Thalassaemia reduces globin chains instead, producing many small cells with preserved count. Chronic inflammation sequesters iron through hepcidin, restricting supply despite adequate stores.
additionalDifferentials: Iron deficiency versus anaemia of chronic disease
additionalInvestigations: Ferritin with full iron studies and inflammatory markers
Mentzer index and red cell distribution width from the blood count
Haemoglobin electrophoresis when thalassaemia trait is suspected
